text:
Aisha Gomez: hey folks — opening my first change in the monorepo. two quick things: do we require signed commits or a DCO? and any special steps when touching multiple packages? also what should I put in the PR description?

Marco Ruiz: welcome Aisha! short answers: 1) use `git commit --signoff` to add a DCO sign-off (we check for it in CI). 2) if you touch packages in `pkg/` add a changeset (we use changesets to generate release notes). 3) PR description = summary, why, test plan, rollout notes, and link to any related ticket.

Marco Ruiz: branch naming we use: `feat/<team>/<short>` or `fix/<team>/<short>`. example: `feat/runtime/add-kv-cache-metrics`. keep under 4 words after slashes.

Aisha Gomez: thanks — how do I add a changeset?

Nadia Patel: run `yarn changeset` from repo root, choose the package(s) and bump type (patch/minor/major). that commits a tiny file to `.changeset/` which CI reads. quick command:
```
yarn install --frozen-lockfile
yarn changeset // follow prompt
git add .changeset/* && git commit -m "chore(changeset): release note for pkg-xyz" --signoff
```

CI-bot: Heads-up: CI checks you'll see: pre-commit hooks, ruff/black lint, unit tests, mypy, changeset validation, and if `pkg/serving` changed we run infra smoke tests on the dedicated pipeline. Logs posted to the PR by GitHub Actions.

Marco Ruiz: commit message format: `type(scope): short summary` — e.g. `telemetry(runtime): add request_duration metric`. keep header <= 50 chars. Add a longer body after a blank line if needed.

Aisha Gomez: are we strict about merge method? squash/rebase/merge?

Marco Ruiz: preferred: squash-and-merge for small bugfixes and docs. For larger features or multi-commit refactors, keep commits and choose "Rebase and merge" only if history matters — otherwise squash is fine. don't force-push to `main` or shared branches.

Nadia Patel: also watch CODEOWNERS: touching `pkg/serving/*` auto-requests @eng-runtime, `infra/` triggers @eng-infra, and `api/` hits @eng-platform. if you need an extra reviewer ping them in the PR body.

Aisha Gomez: gotcha. for local checks, any shortcuts so I don't run the whole CI?

Marco Ruiz: run pre-commit locally: `pre-commit run --all-files`. run unit tests for impacted packages: `pytest pkg/telemetry/tests -q` or `tox -e py` if you need env parity. for typechecks `poetry run mypy pkg/whatever`. we try to keep the fast loop small.

CI-bot: Note: flaky tests should be annotated with `@flaky` marker and have an issue filed. If CI flakes, add `ci:rerun` label to trigger maintenance job.

Aisha Gomez: any docs I should link in the PR?

Marco Ruiz: yes: link to PR checklist (internal) and our contributing guide. paste this: https://redwood.example/docs/pr-checklist and check the "changeset" and "tests" boxes before requesting reviews.

onboard-bot: Reminder: new contributors—drop a short intro in #new-hires and include a link to your PR for extra reviews :wave:

Aisha Gomez: thanks all — I'll add a changeset, sign off commits, and tag codeowners when I push. appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:
